# Waypoint — Full Documentation

> Schema-driven multi-step journey framework for React & Next.js



---

# Waypoint

**Schema-driven multi-step journey framework for React & Next.js**

Waypoint turns complex multi-step flows (onboarding, checkout, wizards) into a portable JSON schema you can build visually, validate strictly, and render anywhere.

## How it works

1. **Define a schema** — steps, fields, validation rules, and visibility conditions in a single `WaypointSchema` JSON object
2. **Render with WaypointRunner** — the provider initialises a Zustand store, handles persistence and deep-link resume
3. **Use hooks in each step** — `useWaypointStep()` gives you a react-hook-form instance pre-wired to the step's Zod schema

The schema is self-contained. Export it, commit it, pass it as a prop — Waypoint is stateless until you mount a runner.

## Packages

| Package | Description |
|---|---|
| `@waypoint/core` | Schema types · condition engine · tree resolver · Zustand runtime store · Zod generator |
| `@waypoint/react` | Headless hooks (`useWaypoint`, `useWaypointStep`) — router-agnostic |
| `@waypoint/next` | Next.js App Router integration (`WaypointRunner`, `useWaypointStep` with RHF + Zod) |
| `@waypoint/builder` | Embeddable no-code UI for building and testing schemas |

## Quick install

```bash
# Next.js App Router
pnpm add @waypoint/next @waypoint/core

# Plain React (any router)
pnpm add @waypoint/react @waypoint/core
```

## Minimal example

```tsx
// 1. Define a schema (or generate one with <WaypointBuilder>)
const schema: WaypointSchema = {
  version: "1",
  id: "onboarding",
  name: "User Onboarding",
  steps: [
    {
      id: "personal",
      title: "Personal info",
      url: "/onboarding/personal",
      fields: [
        { id: "name",  type: "text",  label: "Full name",  validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }] },
        { id: "email", type: "email", label: "Email address", validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }, { type: "email", message: "Invalid email" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "confirm",
      title: "Confirm",
      url: "/onboarding/confirm",
      fields: [],
    },
  ],
};

// 2. Wrap your pages with WaypointRunner
// app/onboarding/layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <WaypointRunner schema={schema} onComplete={(data) => console.log(data)}>
      {children}
    </WaypointRunner>
  );
}

// 3. In each step page
// app/onboarding/personal/page.tsx
export default function PersonalPage() {
  const { fields, form, handleSubmit, progress, isFirstStep } = useWaypointStep();
  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <progress value={progress} max={100} />
      {fields.map((f) => (
        <input key={f.definition.id} {...form.register(f.definition.id)} />
      ))}
      <button type="submit">Continue →</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

[Get started →](/getting-started)

# Getting Started

## Installation



`zustand` is a peer dependency of `@waypoint/core`. It is installed automatically by most package managers.

---

## Step 1 — Define your schema

A `WaypointSchema` describes every step, field, validation rule and visibility condition in your journey.

```ts
// lib/onboarding.schema.ts


export const onboardingSchema: WaypointSchema = {
  version: "1",
  id: "onboarding",
  name: "User Onboarding",
  steps: [
    {
      id: "personal",
      title: "Personal info",
      url: "/onboarding/personal",
      fields: [
        {
          id: "name",
          type: "text",
          label: "Full name",
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Name is required" }],
        },
        {
          id: "email",
          type: "email",
          label: "Email address",
          validation: [
            { type: "required", message: "Email is required" },
            { type: "email",    message: "Must be a valid email" },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "company",
      title: "Company",
      url: "/onboarding/company",
      // This step only appears when the user selects "professional"
      visibleWhen: {
        combinator: "and",
        rules: [{ field: "personal.accountType", operator: "equals", value: "professional" }],
      },
      fields: [
        { id: "companyName", type: "text", label: "Company name",
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "confirm",
      title: "Review & confirm",
      url: "/onboarding/confirm",
      fields: [],
    },
  ],
};
```

You can build schemas visually with `<WaypointBuilder>` instead of writing JSON by hand. See the [Builder guide](/guides/builder).

---

## Step 2 — Add WaypointRunner to your layout

`WaypointRunner` is a React provider that creates an isolated Zustand store for your journey and handles init, persistence and callbacks.

```tsx
// app/onboarding/layout.tsx
"use client";




export default function OnboardingLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  async function handleComplete(data: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>) {
    await fetch("/api/onboarding", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(data) });
    router.push("/dashboard");
  }

  return (
    <WaypointRunner schema={onboardingSchema} onComplete={handleComplete}>
      {children}
    </WaypointRunner>
  );
}
```

---

## Step 3 — Use `useWaypointStep` in each page

`useWaypointStep()` auto-detects the current step from the URL, returns the visible fields, and provides a react-hook-form instance pre-wired to the step's Zod validation schema.

```tsx
// app/onboarding/personal/page.tsx
"use client";



export default function PersonalPage() {
  const { fields, form, handleSubmit, goBack, progress, isFirstStep, isLastStep } =
    useWaypointStep();

  return (
    
      {/* Progress bar */}
      

      <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(handleSubmit)}>
        {fields.map((field) => (
          
            <label>{field.definition.label}</label>
            <input
              type={field.definition.type}
              placeholder={field.definition.placeholder}
              {...form.register(field.definition.id)}
            />
            {form.formState.errors[field.definition.id] && (
              <span>{String(form.formState.errors[field.definition.id]?.message)}</span>
            )}
          
        ))}

        {!isFirstStep && (
          <button type="button" onClick={goBack}>← Back</button>
        )}
        <button type="submit">
          {isLastStep ? "Finish ✓" : "Continue →"}
        </button>
      </form>
    
  );
}
```

The same component works for **every step** — fields are resolved dynamically from the schema. You only need one page component per step if your fields are similar enough.

---

## Step 4 — Set up routes

Each step's `url` in your schema must match a Next.js route. For the schema above:

```
app/onboarding/
├── layout.tsx          ← WaypointRunner lives here
├── personal/
│   └── page.tsx        ← step id: "personal"
├── company/
│   └── page.tsx        ← step id: "company" (conditional)
└── confirm/
    └── page.tsx        ← step id: "confirm"
```

`useWaypointStep()` matches the current `pathname` to the step `url`, so each page automatically knows which step it is.

# WaypointSchema

The `WaypointSchema` is the single source of truth for a journey. It is a plain JSON object describing every step, field, validation rule, condition and external variable. It is portable — export it, commit it, and pass it as a prop to `WaypointRunner` or `WaypointBuilder`.

## Top-level shape

```ts
interface WaypointSchema {
  version: "1";
  id: string;                           // unique journey identifier
  name: string;                         // display name
  steps: StepDefinition[];
  externalVariables?: ExternalVariable[];
  customTypes?: CustomTypeDefinition[];
  persistenceMode?: PersistenceMode;    // "zustand" | "backend-step" | "backend-manual"
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

## StepDefinition

```ts
interface StepDefinition {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  url: string;                    // URL for this step — e.g. "/onboarding/personal"
  fields: FieldDefinition[];
  visibleWhen?: ConditionGroup;   // hide/show the entire step based on data
  enableResumeFromHere?: boolean; // mark as a valid deep-link entry point
}
```

Steps are ordered. `resolveTree()` evaluates `visibleWhen` on each step against current form data to produce the list of steps actually presented to the user.

## FieldDefinition

```ts
interface FieldDefinition {
  id: string;
  type: FieldType;               // "text" | "email" | "select" | ...
  label: string;
  placeholder?: string;
  defaultValue?: unknown;
  options?: SelectOption[];      // for select / multiselect / radio
  validation?: ValidationRule[];
  visibleWhen?: ConditionGroup;  // field-level visibility
  dependsOn?: string[];          // dot-paths: "stepId.fieldId" or "$ext.varId"
}
```

### Built-in field types

| Type | Input |
|---|---|
| `text` `email` `password` `tel` `url` `number` `date` | `<input type="…">` |
| `textarea` | `<textarea>` |
| `select` | `<select>` |
| `multiselect` | `<select multiple>` |
| `radio` | `<input type="radio">` group |
| `checkbox` | `<input type="checkbox">` |
| `file` | `<input type="file">` |

Custom types can be added to the schema via `customTypes` and registered in the builder.

## ValidationRule

```ts
interface ValidationRule {
  type: "required" | "min" | "max" | "minLength" | "maxLength"
      | "email" | "url" | "regex" | "custom";
  value?: string | number;    // for min/max/minLength/maxLength/regex
  message: string;            // error text shown to the user
  customValidatorId?: string; // for "custom" — id registered at runtime
}
```

`buildZodSchema(fields)` from `@waypoint/core` converts these rules into a Zod object schema automatically. `useWaypointStep()` in `@waypoint/next` uses this schema to drive react-hook-form validation.

## ExternalVariable

Variables whose values come from outside the journey (session data, API response, URL params) that conditions can reference as `$ext.varId`.

```ts
interface ExternalVariable {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  type: "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "object";
  blocking: boolean;        // if true and value is missing, runner blocks rendering
  usedIn?: Array<{ stepId: string; fieldId?: string }>;
}
```

Pass values via `WaypointRunner`'s `externalVars` prop.

## PersistenceMode

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"zustand"` | Zustand persist middleware writes to `localStorage`. State resumes on reload. |
| `"backend-step"` | `onStepComplete` is called after every step — persist server-side per step. |
| `"backend-manual"` | You control when to persist via `onDataChange`. |

## Example — conditional step

```ts
const schema: WaypointSchema = {
  version: "1",
  id: "insurance",
  name: "Insurance Quote",
  steps: [
    {
      id: "basics",
      title: "Basic info",
      url: "/quote/basics",
      fields: [
        { id: "age", type: "number", label: "Your age",
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "senior",
      title: "Senior options",
      url: "/quote/senior",
      // Only shown when age >= 65
      visibleWhen: {
        combinator: "and",
        rules: [{ field: "basics.age", operator: "greaterThanOrEqual", value: 65 }],
      },
      fields: [
        { id: "healthPlan", type: "select", label: "Health plan",
          options: [{ label: "Basic", value: "basic" }, { label: "Extended", value: "extended" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "summary",
      title: "Summary",
      url: "/quote/summary",
      fields: [],
    },
  ],
};
```

See [Conditions](/concepts/progress) for the full list of operators and how to compose groups.

---

# Tree Resolution

The **resolved tree** is the computed list of steps and fields that are actually visible to the user at a given moment, after evaluating all conditions against the current form data and external variables.

## resolveTree()

```ts


const tree: ResolvedTree = resolveTree(schema, data, externalVars);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `WaypointSchema` | The journey definition |
| `data` | `Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>` | Form data: `{ stepId: { fieldId: value } }` |
| `externalVars` | `Record<string, unknown>` | External variable values |

### ResolvedTree

```ts
interface ResolvedTree {
  steps: ResolvedStep[];          // visible steps, in order
  hiddenSteps: ResolvedStep[];    // steps whose visibleWhen evaluated to false
  missingExternalVars: string[];  // blocking external variables that have no value
}

interface ResolvedStep {
  definition: StepDefinition;
  visible: boolean;
  fields: ResolvedField[];        // all fields, including hidden ones
}

interface ResolvedField {
  definition: FieldDefinition;
  visible: boolean;               // after evaluating field-level visibleWhen
  dependenciesMet: boolean;       // all dependsOn paths have a value
}
```

`resolveTree()` is a **pure function** — it has no side effects and takes no React context. You can call it anywhere: in hooks, server components, tests, or plain scripts.

## Navigation helpers

After resolving the tree you can navigate it with these helpers:

```ts


// Next step after currentStepId (undefined if on last step)
const next = getNextStep(tree.steps, currentStepId);

// Previous step before currentStepId (undefined if on first step)
const prev = getPreviousStep(tree.steps, currentStepId);

// 0–100 progress based on position in the visible tree
const pct = calculateProgress(tree.steps, currentStepId);

// Deepest step the user can navigate to given their data
const lastValid = findLastValidStep(tree.steps, data, externalVars);
```

## When the tree changes

Conditions are re-evaluated every time data changes. If a user's answer makes a previously hidden step visible — or hides a step they already visited — the tree updates immediately.

`useWaypointStep()` in `@waypoint/next` handles this automatically:
1. After the user submits a step, the tree is re-resolved with the new data
2. If the set of visible step IDs changed, `truncateHistoryAt(stepId)` prunes stale forward history
3. Navigation then proceeds to the first step of the new tree

## Runtime store integration

The runtime store (`createRuntimeStore`) calls `resolveTree` internally via the computed helpers:

```ts


const store = createRuntimeStore();
store.getState().init(schema);

// Computed (not stored) — always derives from current state
const tree    = getResolvedTree(store.getState());
const current = getCurrentStep(store.getState());
```

These helpers are thin wrappers around `resolveTree()` that read `schema`, `data`, and `externalVars` directly from state.

## Example — tree with hidden step

```ts
const schema = { /* insurance schema with "senior" step */ };

// User is 30 — "senior" step is hidden
const tree1 = resolveTree(schema, { basics: { age: 30 } }, {});
// tree1.steps = [ "basics", "summary" ]
// tree1.hiddenSteps = [ "senior" ]

// User changed to 70 — "senior" step appears
const tree2 = resolveTree(schema, { basics: { age: 70 } }, {});
// tree2.steps = [ "basics", "senior", "summary" ]
// tree2.hiddenSteps = []
```

---

# Conditions

Conditions control the visibility of steps and fields. They are evaluated by `resolveTree()` every time the journey data changes. A step or field with no `visibleWhen` is always visible.

## ConditionGroup

```ts
interface ConditionGroup {
  combinator: "and" | "or";
  rules: ConditionRule[];
  groups?: ConditionGroup[];  // nested sub-groups
}

interface ConditionRule {
  field: string;            // dot-path: "stepId.fieldId" or "$ext.varId"
  operator: ConditionOperator;
  value?: unknown;
}
```

Groups can be nested arbitrarily deep. Mixed AND/OR logic is achieved by nesting groups.

## Operators

| Operator | Description | `value` needed |
|---|---|---|
| `equals` | Strict equality | Yes |
| `notEquals` | Strict inequality | Yes |
| `greaterThan` | `field > value` | Yes |
| `greaterThanOrEqual` | `field >= value` | Yes |
| `lessThan` | `field < value` | Yes |
| `lessThanOrEqual` | `field <= value` | Yes |
| `contains` | String includes / array includes | Yes |
| `notContains` | Negation of `contains` | Yes |
| `in` | Field value is in array | Yes (array) |
| `notIn` | Field value is not in array | Yes (array) |
| `exists` | Field has a non-empty value | No |
| `notExists` | Field has no value or is empty | No |
| `matches` | Field matches a regex | Yes (regex string) |

## Field paths

Rules reference data with dot-paths:

| Path format | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `"stepId.fieldId"` | Value of `fieldId` in step `stepId` |
| `"$ext.varId"` | External variable with id `varId` |

## Examples

### Simple required field

```ts
// Show "companyName" field only when account type is "professional"
{
  id: "companyName",
  type: "text",
  label: "Company name",
  visibleWhen: {
    combinator: "and",
    rules: [{ field: "personal.accountType", operator: "equals", value: "professional" }],
  },
}
```

### OR condition

```ts
// Show this step when the user is either a freelancer OR an agency
{
  id: "billing",
  title: "Billing info",
  url: "/billing",
  visibleWhen: {
    combinator: "or",
    rules: [
      { field: "personal.role", operator: "equals", value: "freelancer" },
      { field: "personal.role", operator: "equals", value: "agency" },
    ],
  },
}
```

### Nested AND/OR

```ts
// (age >= 65) AND (country === "FR" OR country === "BE")
{
  combinator: "and",
  rules: [{ field: "basics.age", operator: "greaterThanOrEqual", value: 65 }],
  groups: [
    {
      combinator: "or",
      rules: [
        { field: "basics.country", operator: "equals", value: "FR" },
        { field: "basics.country", operator: "equals", value: "BE" },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
```

### External variable

```ts
// Show premium features only if the user has an active subscription
// (value comes from your API, passed as externalVars to WaypointRunner)
{
  combinator: "and",
  rules: [{ field: "$ext.subscriptionActive", operator: "equals", value: true }],
}
```

## Low-level API

```ts


// Evaluate a group
const result: boolean = evaluateConditionGroup(group, data, externalVars);

// Shorthand — undefined group always returns true
const visible: boolean = isVisible(group, data, externalVars);

// Resolve a dot-path to its current value
const value: unknown = resolveFieldValue("personal.email", data, externalVars);
```

---

# Persistence

Waypoint supports three persistence strategies. The strategy is declared in your schema's `persistenceMode` field and activated by `WaypointRunner`.

## Modes

### `"zustand"` — localStorage (default for SPAs)

When `persistenceMode: "zustand"`, `WaypointRunner` activates the Zustand persist middleware. Journey data is automatically saved to `localStorage` under the key `waypoint-runtime-{schemaId}`.

On the next visit, `WaypointRunner`:
1. Detects the saved state via `hasPersistedState(store, schemaId)`
2. Calls `resume(schema, externalVars)` instead of `init()` — preserving `data`, `currentStepId` and `history`
3. Navigates the user to `findLastValidStep()` — their furthest accessible step given current data

```ts
// schema.ts
export const schema: WaypointSchema = {
  version: "1",
  id: "onboarding",
  name: "User Onboarding",
  persistenceMode: "zustand",  // ← enable localStorage persistence
  steps: [ /* ... */ ],
};
```

Only `{ schemaId, data, currentStepId, history, completed }` are persisted — not the full schema or callbacks. The schema is always re-provided by your app at mount time.

### `"backend-step"` — Server-side, per step

Call your backend after each step completes. Wire up the `onStepComplete` callback on `WaypointRunner`:

```tsx
<WaypointRunner
  schema={schema}
  onStepComplete={async (stepId, stepData) => {
    await api.saveStep(schema.id, stepId, stepData);
  }}
  onComplete={async (allData) => {
    await api.completeJourney(schema.id, allData);
    router.push("/success");
  }}
>
  {children}
</WaypointRunner>
```

### `"backend-manual"` — Server-side, on demand

Use `onDataChange` to receive every data mutation and decide yourself when to persist:

```tsx
<WaypointRunner
  schema={schema}
  onDataChange={(data) => {
    debouncedSave(data);
  }}
>
  {children}
</WaypointRunner>
```

## Resume via `fetchData`

For backend-persisted journeys, pass `fetchData` to `WaypointRunner` to reload saved data on mount:

```tsx
<WaypointRunner
  schema={schema}
  fetchData={async () => {
    const saved = await api.loadJourney(schema.id);
    return saved.data; // Record<stepId, Record<fieldId, value>>
  }}
  onComplete={handleComplete}
>
  {children}
</WaypointRunner>
```

`fetchData` is called once during init. If it returns data, `WaypointRunner` calls `init(schema, { data: fetchedData })` and navigates to `findLastValidStep()`.

## Init vs. Resume

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| No persisted state (first visit) | `init(schema)` — navigate to first step |
| Persisted state found (`"zustand"` mode) | `resume(schema)` — keep data, navigate to last valid step |
| `fetchData` returns data | `init(schema, { data })` — navigate to last valid step |
| External vars changed after mount | `store.setExternalVar(varId, value)` — tree re-resolves automatically |

## Resetting

To restart a journey and clear persisted state:

```ts
// Reset store and navigate back to step 1
store.getState().init(schema);

// Or from a hook
const { reset } = useWaypoint(store);
reset();
```

For `"zustand"` mode this clears both the in-memory store and the localStorage entry.

## Multiple concurrent journeys

Each `<WaypointRunner>` creates its **own isolated store** via `useRef`. You can mount multiple runners simultaneously with no shared state:

```tsx
// Two independent journeys on the same page
<WaypointRunner schema={checkoutSchema}>
  
</WaypointRunner>

<WaypointRunner schema={profileSchema}>
  
</WaypointRunner>
```

Each runner persists under its own key (`waypoint-runtime-checkout` / `waypoint-runtime-profile`).

---

# @waypoint/core

Framework-agnostic engine. Zero React dependency. All other packages build on top of this one.

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/core
```

---

## createRuntimeStore()

Creates an isolated Zustand vanilla store for a single journey.

```ts


const store = createRuntimeStore();
// or with localStorage persistence:
const store = createRuntimeStore({ persistenceMode: "zustand", schemaId: "onboarding" });
```

### Options

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `persistenceMode` | `string` | `"zustand"` activates localStorage persist middleware |
| `schemaId` | `string` | Used as part of the localStorage key: `waypoint-runtime-{schemaId}` |

### Store state

```ts
interface WaypointRuntimeState {
  schema: WaypointSchema | null;
  data: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>; // { stepId: { fieldId: value } }
  externalVars: Record<string, unknown>;
  currentStepId: string | null;
  history: string[];      // step IDs visited in order
  isSubmitting: boolean;
  completed: boolean;
}
```

### Store actions

| Action | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | `(schema, options?) => void` | Fresh start — resets all navigation state |
| `resume` | `(schema, externalVars?) => void` | Update schema/vars, keep data and navigation |
| `setFieldValue` | `(stepId, fieldId, value) => void` | Set a single field |
| `setStepData` | `(stepId, data) => void` | Replace all data for a step |
| `setExternalVar` | `(varId, value) => void` | Set an external variable |
| `setCurrentStep` | `(stepId) => void` | Navigate to a step |
| `truncateHistoryAt` | `(stepId) => void` | Remove all history after stepId |
| `reset` | `() => void` | Clear all state |

---

## resolveTree()

Pure function — evaluates all conditions and returns the visible tree.

```ts


const tree = resolveTree(schema, data, externalVars);
// { steps: ResolvedStep[], hiddenSteps: ResolvedStep[], missingExternalVars: string[] }
```

See [Tree Resolution](/concepts/history) for full documentation.

---

## Navigation helpers

```ts


getNextStep(steps, currentStepId)      // ResolvedStep | undefined
getPreviousStep(steps, currentStepId)  // ResolvedStep | undefined
calculateProgress(steps, currentStepId) // number (0–100)
findLastValidStep(steps, data, externalVars) // ResolvedStep | undefined
```

---

## buildZodSchema()

Generates a Zod validation schema from an array of resolved fields.

```ts


const zodSchema = buildZodSchema(fields); // z.ZodObject
const result = zodSchema.safeParse(formValues);
```

Supported validation rules: `required`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `email`, `url`, `regex`, `custom`.

```ts
// Register a custom validator before using it


registerCustomValidator("strongPassword", (value) => {
  return typeof value === "string" && value.length >= 8 && /\d/.test(value);
});
```

---

## Condition functions

```ts


// Evaluate a ConditionGroup
evaluateConditionGroup(group, data, externalVars) // boolean

// Shorthand — undefined returns true
isVisible(group, data, externalVars)              // boolean

// Resolve a dot-path to its value
resolveFieldValue("stepId.fieldId", data, externalVars) // unknown
```

---

## validateSchema()

```ts


const result = validateSchema(parsed);
// { valid: boolean, errors?: string[] }

assertSchema(parsed); // throws if invalid
```

---

## Computed state helpers

These are thin wrappers around `resolveTree()` that read directly from a store state object:

```ts

  getResolvedTree,
  getCurrentStep,
  getNextStepFromState,
  getPreviousStepFromState,
  calculateProgressFromState,
  getMissingBlockingVars,
} from "@waypoint/core";

const state = store.getState();
getResolvedTree(state)             // ResolvedTree
getCurrentStep(state)              // ResolvedStep | undefined
getNextStepFromState(state)        // ResolvedStep | undefined
getPreviousStepFromState(state)    // ResolvedStep | undefined
calculateProgressFromState(state)  // number (0–100)
getMissingBlockingVars(state)      // string[]
```

---

## hasPersistedState()

```ts


// Returns true if localStorage has valid state for this schema
hasPersistedState(store, schemaId) // boolean
```

Used internally by `WaypointRunner` to decide whether to call `resume()` or `init()`.

---

# @waypoint/react

Headless React hooks that take a `StoreApi` instance and work with any router.

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/react @waypoint/core
```

If you are using Next.js App Router, prefer `@waypoint/next` which provides `WaypointRunner` and a `useWaypointStep()` that auto-wires react-hook-form, Zod validation and navigation.

---

## useWaypoint()

Access full journey state and actions.

```ts



const state = useWaypoint(store);
```

### Parameter

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `store` | `StoreApi<WaypointRuntimeStore>` | Store instance from `createRuntimeStore()` |

### Return value

```ts
interface WaypointState {
  schema: WaypointSchema | null;
  data: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>;
  externalVars: Record<string, unknown>;
  currentStepId: string | null;
  currentStep: ResolvedStep | undefined;
  nextStep: ResolvedStep | undefined;
  previousStep: ResolvedStep | undefined;
  tree: ResolvedTree;
  progress: number;             // 0–100
  isFirstStep: boolean;
  isLastStep: boolean;
  isSubmitting: boolean;
  missingExternalVars: string[];

  // Actions (delegates to store.getState())
  setFieldValue(stepId: string, fieldId: string, value: unknown): void;
  setStepData(stepId: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): void;
  setExternalVar(varId: string, value: unknown): void;
  setCurrentStep(stepId: string): void;
  reset(): void;
}
```

### Example

```tsx




function MyJourneyShell({ schema, children }) {
  const storeRef = useRef(createRuntimeStore());

  useEffect(() => {
    storeRef.current.getState().init(schema);
  }, [schema]);

  const { currentStep, progress, setCurrentStep } = useWaypoint(storeRef.current);

  return (
    
      
      <h1>{currentStep?.definition.title}</h1>
      {children}
    
  );
}
```

---

## useWaypointStep()

Access the fields and data for a specific step.

```ts


const step = useWaypointStep(store, stepId);
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `store` | `StoreApi<WaypointRuntimeStore>` | Store instance |
| `stepId` | `string` | ID of the step to resolve |

### Return value

```ts
interface WaypointHeadlessStep {
  step: ResolvedStep | undefined;
  fields: ResolvedField[];          // visible fields only
  stepData: Record<string, unknown>; // current data for this step
  setFieldValue(fieldId: string, value: unknown): void;
  setStepData(data: Record<string, unknown>): void;
}
```

### Example

```tsx
function PersonalStep({ store }) {
  const { fields, stepData, setFieldValue } = useWaypointStep(store, "personal");

  return (
    <form>
      {fields.map((field) => (
        <input
          key={field.definition.id}
          value={(stepData[field.definition.id] as string) ?? ""}
          onChange={(e) => setFieldValue(field.definition.id, e.target.value)}
          placeholder={field.definition.placeholder}
        />
      ))}
    </form>
  );
}
```

---

## Usage pattern — headless with custom router

When you need to integrate with a router other than Next.js, build on top of `useWaypoint` and `useWaypointStep`:

```tsx




function WaypointProvider({ schema, children }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const storeRef = useRef(createRuntimeStore());

  useEffect(() => {
    storeRef.current.getState().init(schema);
  }, [schema]);

  const { tree, currentStepId } = useWaypoint(storeRef.current);

  function goNext() {
    const next = getNextStep(tree.steps, currentStepId ?? "");
    if (next) {
      storeRef.current.getState().setCurrentStep(next.definition.id);
      navigate(next.definition.url);
    }
  }

  return (
    <StoreContext.Provider value={{ store: storeRef.current, goNext }}>
      {children}
    </StoreContext.Provider>
  );
}
```

---

# @waypoint/next

Next.js App Router integration. Provides `WaypointRunner` (context provider) and `useWaypointStep` (per-page hook with react-hook-form + Zod).

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/next @waypoint/core
```

---

## \<WaypointRunner\>

A React provider that initialises an isolated Zustand store, handles persistence, deep-link resume and exposes callbacks for data lifecycle events.

```tsx


<WaypointRunner
  schema={schema}
  externalVars={{ userId: "42" }}
  onComplete={async (data) => { /* save data, redirect */ }}
  onStepComplete={async (stepId, stepData) => { /* per-step save */ }}
  onDataChange={(data) => { /* any field changed */ }}
>
  {children}
</WaypointRunner>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `WaypointSchema` | ✓ | The journey definition |
| `externalVars` | `Record<string, unknown>` | | External variable values referenced by conditions |
| `defaultValues` | `Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>` | | Pre-populated form data |
| `fetchData` | `() => Promise<Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>>` | | Async loader for saved data — called once on mount |
| `onComplete` | `(data) => void \| Promise<void>` | | Called when the last step is submitted |
| `onStepComplete` | `(stepId, stepData) => void \| Promise<void>` | | Called after each step is validated and submitted |
| `onDataChange` | `(data) => void` | | Called on every field value change |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` | ✓ | Step pages |

### Init / Resume logic

On mount, `WaypointRunner`:

1. Creates a store via `createRuntimeStore({ persistenceMode, schemaId })`
2. If `persistenceMode === "zustand"` and `hasPersistedState(store, schemaId)` → calls `resume(schema, externalVars)`
3. Otherwise → calls `init(schema, { data: defaultValues || fetchData() })`
4. After init, if data is present → navigates to `findLastValidStep()` (deep-link resume)

When `externalVars` prop changes after mount, the runner calls `store.setExternalVar()` for each changed key — the tree re-resolves automatically.

`WaypointRunner` must be a **Client Component** (`"use client"`). Place it in a layout file, not a page.

---

## useWaypointStep()

Per-page hook that auto-detects the current step from the URL, provides a react-hook-form instance pre-configured with the step's Zod schema, and handles validation + navigation on submit.

```tsx


const {
  currentStep,
  fields,
  form,
  handleSubmit,
  goBack,
  progress,
  isFirstStep,
  isLastStep,
  isSubmitting,
  errors,
} = useWaypointStep();
```

Must be called inside a component that is a descendant of `<WaypointRunner>`.

### Return value

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `currentStep` | `ResolvedStep \| undefined` | The step matched to the current URL |
| `fields` | `ResolvedField[]` | Visible fields for this step |
| `form` | `UseFormReturn` | react-hook-form instance — pre-wired to Zod schema |
| `handleSubmit` | `() => Promise<void>` | Validate → persist → navigate |
| `goBack` | `() => void` | Navigate to previous step |
| `progress` | `number` | 0–100 based on position in visible tree |
| `isFirstStep` | `boolean` | No previous step in resolved tree |
| `isLastStep` | `boolean` | No next step in resolved tree |
| `isSubmitting` | `boolean` | True while handleSubmit is running |
| `errors` | `FieldErrors` | react-hook-form validation errors |

### handleSubmit flow

1. Validate form via react-hook-form + Zod (built from `buildZodSchema(fields)`)
2. Persist step data into the store: `store.setStepData(stepId, values)`
3. Re-resolve tree with new data
4. If visible step IDs changed → `truncateHistoryAt(stepId)` (prevents stale forward history)
5. Call `onDataChange` callback
6. Call `onStepComplete` callback (awaited)
7. If more steps → navigate to `next.definition.url` via `router.push()`
8. If last step → call `onComplete(allData)`

### Example — full step page

```tsx
// app/onboarding/personal/page.tsx
"use client";



export default function PersonalPage() {
  const { fields, form, handleSubmit, goBack, progress, isFirstStep, isLastStep } =
    useWaypointStep();

  return (
    
      {/* Progress */}
      
        
      

      <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(handleSubmit)} className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        {fields.map((field) => (
          
            <label className="block text-sm font-medium mb-1">
              {field.definition.label}
            </label>
            <input
              type={field.definition.type}
              className="w-full border rounded px-3 py-2"
              placeholder={field.definition.placeholder}
              {...form.register(field.definition.id)}
            />
            {form.formState.errors[field.definition.id] && (
              <p className="text-red-500 text-xs mt-1">
                {String(form.formState.errors[field.definition.id]?.message)}
              </p>
            )}
          
        ))}

        
          {!isFirstStep && (
            <button type="button" onClick={goBack} className="px-4 py-2 border rounded">
              ← Back
            </button>
          )}
          <button type="submit" className="px-6 py-2 bg-blue-600 text-white rounded">
            {isLastStep ? "Finish ✓" : "Continue →"}
          </button>
        
      </form>
    
  );
}
```

---

## useWaypointRuntimeContext()

Access the raw `WaypointRunner` context from any descendant component.

```ts


const { schema, store, onComplete, onStepComplete, onDataChange } =
  useWaypointRuntimeContext();
```

Returns `WaypointRuntimeContextValue`:

```ts
interface WaypointRuntimeContextValue {
  schema: WaypointSchema;
  store: StoreApi<WaypointRuntimeStore>;
  onComplete?: (data: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>) => void | Promise<void>;
  onStepComplete?: (stepId: string, data: Record<string, unknown>) => void | Promise<void>;
  onDataChange?: (data: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>) => void;
}
```

Useful when you need direct store access alongside `useWaypoint()` from `@waypoint/react`.

---

# @waypoint/builder

An embeddable no-code UI for building and testing `WaypointSchema` objects. Drop it into any React or Next.js app.

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/builder @waypoint/core
```

---

## \<WaypointBuilder\>

A self-contained editor component that renders a 3-column layout (step list, field list, step/field editors) and exports a `WaypointSchema`.

```tsx


<WaypointBuilder
  defaultValue={existingSchema}
  onChange={(schema) => console.log(schema)}
  onSave={async (schema) => {
    await fetch("/api/schemas", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(schema) });
  }}
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultValue` | `WaypointSchema` | | Initial schema to load |
| `onChange` | `(schema: WaypointSchema) => void` | | Called on every change |
| `onSave` | `(schema: WaypointSchema) => void \| Promise<void>` | | Called when user clicks "Save" |
| `theme` | `WaypointTheme` | | Custom theme (colors, fonts) |
| `className` | `string` | | CSS class on the root element |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` | | Inline style on the root element |

### Layout

The builder renders in a **3-column layout**:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Left | Step list + External Variables panel |
| Centre | Field list for the selected step |
| Right | Step editor (title, URL, conditions) + Field editor |

The builder requires explicit dimensions — set `height: 100%` on a sized parent or use `style={{ height: "100vh" }}` for full-screen.

### Preview mode

Clicking **▶ Tester** in the toolbar switches to a **split view**:

- **Left panel** — resolved step list with status icons: `✓` done · `→` current · `○` upcoming · `–` hidden
- **Right panel** — live step renderer with field inputs, inline validation, progress bar, and Prev/Next navigation

Click **← Éditer** to return to the builder. The preview uses an isolated in-memory store — no localStorage, no side effects.

### Theme

```ts


// Pass a partial theme to override specific tokens

```

Built-in themes: `DEFAULT_THEME`, `DARK_THEME`. All values are mapped to CSS custom properties at the root element.

---

## useBuilderStore

Access the builder's internal Zustand store for programmatic control.

```ts


const { schema, loadSchema, isDirty, resetSchema } = useBuilderStore();
```

### Useful methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `loadSchema(schema)` | Load a schema into the builder |
| `resetSchema()` | Reset to the empty default schema |

`useBuilderStore` is a singleton — there can only be one builder instance per page. For multiple builders, you'd need to isolate each in its own React root.

---

## Embedding in Next.js

```tsx
// app/admin/builder/page.tsx
"use client";




export default function BuilderPage() {
  const router = useRouter();

  return (
    
      <WaypointBuilder
        onSave={async (schema) => {
          const res = await fetch("/api/journey-schemas", {
            method: "POST",
            headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
            body: JSON.stringify(schema),
          });
          if (res.ok) router.push("/admin/journeys");
        }}
      />
    
  );
}
```

## Loading an existing schema

```tsx
"use client";





export default function EditSchemaPage({ params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
  const [schema, setSchema] = useState<WaypointSchema | undefined>();

  useEffect(() => {
    fetch(`/api/journey-schemas/${params.id}`)
      .then((r) => r.json())
      .then(setSchema);
  }, [params.id]);

  if (!schema) return Loading…;

  return (
    
      <WaypointBuilder
        defaultValue={schema}
        onSave={async (updated) => {
          await fetch(`/api/journey-schemas/${params.id}`, {
            method: "PUT",
            body: JSON.stringify(updated),
          });
        }}
      />
    
  );
}
```

# Next.js Integration

A complete guide to integrating Waypoint in a Next.js App Router project.

## Prerequisites

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/next @waypoint/core
```

## File structure

```
app/
├── onboarding/
│   ├── layout.tsx       ← WaypointRunner lives here
│   ├── personal/
│   │   └── page.tsx     ← step "personal"
│   ├── company/
│   │   └── page.tsx     ← step "company" (conditional)
│   └── confirm/
│       └── page.tsx     ← step "confirm"
└── dashboard/
    └── page.tsx
```

Each step's `url` in your schema must exactly match its Next.js route path.

---

## 1. Define the schema

```ts
// lib/onboarding.schema.ts


export const onboardingSchema: WaypointSchema = {
  version: "1",
  id: "onboarding",
  name: "User Onboarding",
  persistenceMode: "zustand",   // auto-save to localStorage
  steps: [
    {
      id: "personal",
      title: "Personal info",
      url: "/onboarding/personal",
      fields: [
        { id: "firstName", type: "text",  label: "First name",
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }] },
        { id: "email",     type: "email", label: "Email",
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }, { type: "email", message: "Invalid email" }] },
        { id: "accountType", type: "select", label: "Account type",
          options: [{ label: "Personal", value: "personal" }, { label: "Professional", value: "professional" }],
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "company",
      title: "Company details",
      url: "/onboarding/company",
      // Only shown when accountType === "professional"
      visibleWhen: {
        combinator: "and",
        rules: [{ field: "personal.accountType", operator: "equals", value: "professional" }],
      },
      fields: [
        { id: "companyName", type: "text", label: "Company name",
          validation: [{ type: "required", message: "Required" }] },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "confirm",
      title: "Confirm",
      url: "/onboarding/confirm",
      fields: [],
    },
  ],
};
```

---

## 2. Add WaypointRunner to the layout

```tsx
// app/onboarding/layout.tsx
"use client";





export default function OnboardingLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const router = useRouter();

  return (
    <WaypointRunner
      schema={onboardingSchema}
      onStepComplete={async (stepId, stepData) => {
        // Optional: persist to your backend after each step
        await fetch(`/api/draft-steps/${stepId}`, {
          method: "POST",
          body: JSON.stringify(stepData),
        });
      }}
      onComplete={async (data) => {
        await fetch("/api/complete-onboarding", {
          method: "POST",
          body: JSON.stringify(data),
        });
        router.push("/dashboard");
      }}
    >
      
        {children}
      
    </WaypointRunner>
  );
}
```

---

## 3. Create step pages

All step pages look the same — `useWaypointStep()` resolves fields from the schema automatically.

```tsx
// app/onboarding/personal/page.tsx  (same pattern for every step)
"use client";



export default function PersonalPage() {
  const { fields, form, handleSubmit, goBack, progress, isFirstStep, isLastStep } =
    useWaypointStep();

  return (
    
      {/* Progress bar */}
      
        
      

      <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(handleSubmit)} className="flex flex-col gap-5">
        {fields.map((field) => (
          
            <label className="block text-sm font-medium mb-1">
              {field.definition.label}
            </label>

            {field.definition.type === "select" ? (
              <select
                className="w-full border rounded-lg px-3 py-2"
                {...form.register(field.definition.id)}
              >
                <option value="">Choose…</option>
                {field.definition.options?.map((opt) => (
                  <option key={String(opt.value)} value={String(opt.value)}>
                    {opt.label}
                  </option>
                ))}
              </select>
            ) : (
              <input
                type={field.definition.type}
                className="w-full border rounded-lg px-3 py-2"
                placeholder={field.definition.placeholder}
                {...form.register(field.definition.id)}
              />
            )}

            {form.formState.errors[field.definition.id] && (
              <p className="text-red-500 text-xs mt-1">
                {String(form.formState.errors[field.definition.id]?.message)}
              </p>
            )}
          
        ))}

        
          {!isFirstStep && (
            <button type="button" onClick={goBack}
              className="px-4 py-2 border rounded-lg text-sm">
              ← Back
            </button>
          )}
          <button type="submit"
            className="flex-1 bg-blue-600 text-white py-2 rounded-lg text-sm font-medium">
            {isLastStep ? "Finish ✓" : "Continue →"}
          </button>
        
      </form>
    
  );
}
```

---

## 4. Passing external variables

If conditions reference `$ext.varId`, pass values via the `externalVars` prop on `WaypointRunner`.

```tsx
"use client";




export default function Layout({ children }) {
  const { data: session } = useSession();

  return (
    <WaypointRunner
      schema={schema}
      externalVars={{
        userId: session?.user?.id,
        plan: session?.user?.plan,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </WaypointRunner>
  );
}
```

`WaypointRunner` syncs `externalVars` into the store whenever the prop changes. The tree re-resolves automatically.

---

## Resume on page reload

With `persistenceMode: "zustand"` in your schema, journey data is persisted to `localStorage` automatically. When the user returns:

1. `WaypointRunner` detects the saved state
2. Calls `resume()` to restore data without re-initialising
3. Navigates to the last valid step

No additional code needed.

---

# React Integration (Headless)

Use `@waypoint/react` when you need router-agnostic hooks — React Router, TanStack Router, or a custom navigation layer.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/react @waypoint/core
```

## Architecture

Unlike `@waypoint/next`, the headless package ships no provider component. You manage:
- Creating and storing the store instance
- Calling `init()` or `resume()` on mount
- Navigating between steps with your router

## Basic setup

```tsx
// contexts/journey-context.tsx
"use client";





const JourneyContext = createContext<RuntimeStore | null>(null);

export function JourneyProvider({
  schema,
  children,
}: {
  schema: WaypointSchema;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  const storeRef = useRef<RuntimeStore | null>(null);
  if (!storeRef.current) {
    storeRef.current = createRuntimeStore();
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    storeRef.current!.getState().init(schema);
  }, [schema.id]);

  return (
    <JourneyContext.Provider value={storeRef.current}>
      {children}
    </JourneyContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useJourneyStore() {
  const store = useContext(JourneyContext);
  if (!store) throw new Error("useJourneyStore must be used inside <JourneyProvider>");
  return store;
}
```

## Using the hooks

```tsx
// components/StepShell.tsx




export function StepShell({ stepId, children }) {
  const store = useJourneyStore();
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  const {
    currentStep,
    nextStep,
    previousStep,
    progress,
    isFirstStep,
    isLastStep,
    setCurrentStep,
  } = useWaypoint(store);

  function goNext() {
    if (nextStep) {
      setCurrentStep(nextStep.definition.id);
      navigate(nextStep.definition.url);
    }
  }

  function goBack() {
    if (previousStep) {
      setCurrentStep(previousStep.definition.id);
      navigate(previousStep.definition.url);
    }
  }

  return (
    
      
      <h1>{currentStep?.definition.title}</h1>
      {children}
      
        {!isFirstStep && <button onClick={goBack}>← Back</button>}
        {!isLastStep && <button onClick={goNext}>Continue →</button>}
      
    
  );
}
```

## Accessing a specific step's fields

```tsx



function PersonalFields() {
  const store = useJourneyStore();
  const { fields, stepData, setFieldValue } = useWaypointStep(store, "personal");

  return (
    
      {fields.map((field) => (
        <input
          key={field.definition.id}
          value={(stepData[field.definition.id] as string) ?? ""}
          placeholder={field.definition.placeholder}
          onChange={(e) => setFieldValue(field.definition.id, e.target.value)}
        />
      ))}
    
  );
}
```

## Adding validation

Combine `buildZodSchema` with react-hook-form manually:

```tsx





function StepForm({ store, stepId }) {
  const { fields, stepData, setStepData } = useWaypointStep(store, stepId);

  const form = useForm({
    resolver: zodResolver(buildZodSchema(fields)),
    defaultValues: stepData,
  });

  function handleSubmit(values) {
    setStepData(values);
    // then navigate to next step
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(handleSubmit)}>
      {fields.map((field) => (
        <input key={field.definition.id} {...form.register(field.definition.id)} />
      ))}
      <button type="submit">Continue</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

`@waypoint/next`'s `useWaypointStep()` does all of the above automatically. Use the headless approach only when you need control over validation, routing, or form libraries.

## Persistence (manual)

```tsx
// Create store with localStorage persistence
const storeRef = useRef(
  createRuntimeStore({ persistenceMode: "zustand", schemaId: schema.id })
);

useEffect(() => {
  const store = storeRef.current;
  if (hasPersistedState(store, schema.id)) {
    store.getState().resume(schema);
  } else {
    store.getState().init(schema);
  }
}, []);
```

---

# Builder Guide

`@waypoint/builder` provides a no-code UI for creating and editing `WaypointSchema` objects. It is an embeddable React component — drop it into any admin panel or internal tool.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @waypoint/builder @waypoint/core
```

## Basic embed

```tsx
"use client";



export default function BuilderPage() {
  return (
    
      <WaypointBuilder
        onSave={(schema) => {
          console.log("Schema saved:", schema);
        }}
        onChange={(schema) => {
          // Live updates — auto-save drafts, display preview, etc.
        }}
      />
    
  );
}
```

The builder needs an explicit height on its parent container — it fills 100% of the available space.

## Loading an existing schema

Pass a `WaypointSchema` (loaded from your API, a file, or another source) as `defaultValue`:

```tsx
const [schema, setSchema] = useState<WaypointSchema | undefined>();

useEffect(() => {
  fetch(`/api/schemas/${id}`).then((r) => r.json()).then(setSchema);
}, [id]);

if (!schema) return ;

return (
  
    <WaypointBuilder
      defaultValue={schema}
      onSave={async (updated) => {
        await fetch(`/api/schemas/${id}`, {
          method: "PUT",
          body: JSON.stringify(updated),
        });
      }}
    />
  
);
```

## What you can build in the UI

The builder supports the full `WaypointSchema` feature set:

| Feature | Builder UI |
|---|---|
| Steps | Add, rename, reorder, delete |
| Step URL | Editable text input |
| Step conditions | Visual condition builder with AND/OR groups |
| Fields | Add, reorder, configure type, label, placeholder |
| Field type | Dropdown (all 13 built-in types + custom types) |
| Field validation | Add rules (required, email, min/max, regex…) |
| Field conditions | Same visual builder as step conditions |
| External variables | Declare id, type, blocking flag |
| Persistence mode | Dropdown (zustand / backend-step / backend-manual) |

## Preview mode (Test)

Click **▶ Tester** in the toolbar to enter preview mode. This opens a split view:

- **Left** — the resolved step list with live status: `✓` visited, `→` current, `○` upcoming, `–` hidden by condition
- **Right** — a rendered form for the current step with field inputs and validation

This lets you test conditions, validation rules, and step ordering without leaving the builder or writing any code.

Click **← Éditer** to return to the editor at any time.

## Exporting the schema

Click **Export JSON** in the toolbar to download the schema as a `.waypoint.json` file. The file can be imported back into any builder instance.

To export programmatically, read the schema from `onChange` or `onSave`:

```tsx
<WaypointBuilder
  onSave={(schema) => {
    const json = JSON.stringify(schema, null, 2);
    const blob = new Blob([json], { type: "application/json" });
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    // trigger download…
  }}
/>
```

## Validating an imported schema

Use `validateSchema` from `@waypoint/core` to verify a schema before passing it to `defaultValue`:

```ts


const result = validateSchema(parsed);
if (!result.valid) {
  console.error(result.errors);
} else {
  setSchema(parsed);
}
```

## Theming

```tsx


// Use the built-in dark theme


// Or override individual tokens

```

All theme tokens are compiled to CSS custom properties on the root element, so you can also target them with CSS:

```css
.waypoint-builder-root {
  --wp-primary: #6366f1;
  --wp-canvas: #fafafa;
}
```

## Using the generated schema with WaypointRunner

The schema produced by the builder is a standard `WaypointSchema` — use it directly with `WaypointRunner`:

```tsx


// schema loaded from your API (was originally built with WaypointBuilder)
<WaypointRunner schema={schema} onComplete={handleComplete}>
  
</WaypointRunner>
```

No conversion or transformation needed.

# AI & Skills

Use Waypoint documentation with AI agents. Install the Waypoint skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and other AI coding assistants.

---

## LLM-Ready Documentation

Waypoint exposes machine-readable docs compatible with any AI tool that supports the [`llms.txt`](https://llmstxt.org) standard.

| Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|
| [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) | Lightweight index — titles and descriptions of all pages |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) | Complete documentation in plain markdown |

Point your AI assistant at either URL, or paste it directly into context.

---

## Install the Waypoint Skill

The Waypoint skill gives your agent deep knowledge of all four packages — schema types, conditions, hooks, builder API, and real-world patterns — loaded on demand without bloating your context window.



The skill uses **progressive disclosure** — only the name and description are loaded at startup. The full instructions and package references are read only when the agent decides the skill is relevant, keeping context windows efficient.

---

## What's Included

The skill covers all four Waypoint packages with full API references.




**@waypoint/core**

`WaypointSchema` types · `createRuntimeStore()` · `resolveTree()` · `buildZodSchema()` · condition engine · `validateSchema()`



**@waypoint/react**

`useWaypoint()` · `useWaypointStep()` · headless store integration · router-agnostic patterns



**@waypoint/next**

`WaypointRunner` props · `useWaypointStep()` with RHF + Zod · `useWaypointRuntimeContext()` · init vs resume logic



**@waypoint/builder**

`WaypointBuilder` props · `WaypointTheme` tokens · `DEFAULT_THEME` / `DARK_THEME` · `useBuilderStore()` actions




---

## Supported Agents

The skill is distributed via [skills.sh](https://skills.sh) and works with any compatible agent:

**Claude Code** · **Cursor** · **Windsurf** · **OpenCode** · and 40+ others

---

## Verify the Installation

After installing the skill, test it with this prompt:

```
How do I create a multi-step journey with a conditional step that only appears
when the user selects "business" as their account type?
```

A correct response should reference `WaypointSchema` with a `visibleWhen` condition on the step, `WaypointRunner` in a layout file, and `useWaypointStep()` in each page.

---

## Skill Source

The skill lives in the repo at [`.claude/skills/waypoint/`](https://github.com/tmauc/waypoint/tree/master/.claude/skills/waypoint) and is versioned alongside the code. When the API changes, the skill is updated in the same commit.
